subject: Art & Design
title: User Testing: Design with Evidence
description: Learn User Testing: Design with Evidence in one minute.

hook.text: You are not the user. What seems obvious to a designer is often invisible to the audience.

buildup.text: User testing puts real people in front of your design and watches where they succeed and stumble.

discovery.text: Jakob Nielsen proved that testing with just 5 users reveals 85% of usability problems. It doesn't need to be expensive.

twist.text: A/B testing compares two versions with real traffic. Data replaces opinion. The user's behavior is the truth.

climax.text: Designing without testing is decorating. Designing with testing is problem-solving.

punchline.text: Don't ask users what they want. Watch what they do.

quiz.question: How many users does Nielsen say reveal 85% of usability problems?
options: Just 5 users is enough for most usability studies
At least 500 users for statistical significance

details.summary: User testing puts designs in front of real people to observe how they actually interact with them, revealing problems that designers are too close to see. Testing five users catches 85% of usability issues. Evidence-based design decisions outperform designer intuition consistently.
details.whyItMatters: Designers are not their users. What feels intuitive to someone who built the design may be confusing to someone encountering it for the first time. User testing replaces assumptions with evidence, producing designs that actually work.
takeaways: Testing five users catches 85% of usability problems
Real user behavior often contradicts designer assumptions
Evidence-based design consistently outperforms intuition alone

faq.question: How do you run a basic user test?
faq.answer: Give five participants realistic tasks ('Find the product pricing') while observing without helping. Note where they hesitate, click wrong things, or express confusion. Record sessions. Afterward, identify patterns — problems that multiple participants encountered are priority fixes.

faq.question: When should user testing happen in the design process?
faq.answer: As early as possible and as often as budget allows. Testing paper sketches or wireframes is cheaper than testing finished designs. Testing after launch is too late — problems are expensive to fix in production. Even informal hallway testing with colleagues provides valuable signal early on.
